chunks: And among what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿImrān al-Ḥalabī, who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was asked about a man who forgot to fast the three days that were incumbent upon the mutamattiʿ when he did not find the sacrificial offering, until he returned to his family. He said: He should send a blood-offering.

So there is no contradiction between these two reports and the report that we presented earlier from Ibn Miskān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he said: If his companions did not remain with him and he was not able to fast on the road, he should fast ten days when he returns to his family. That is because this is to be understood as referring to one who returned to his family before the end of Dhū al-Ḥijjah, in which case fasting the ten days was permissible for him. But when Dhū al-Ḥijjah has ended, then nothing is permissible for him except the blood-offering, in accordance with what the two reports indicate.

key_terms.الثَّلَاثَةَ الْأَيَّامِ: the three days of fasting required as a substitute
key_terms.الْهَدْيَ: the sacrificial offering required in hajj
key_terms.ذِي الْحِجَّةِ: the month whose end determines the ruling here
key_terms.عَشَرَةَ أَيَّامٍ: the full ten days of substitute fasting
key_terms.يَبْعَثُ بِدَمٍ: he must send a sacrificial blood-offering

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a mutamattiʿ who forgot the substitute fast for the hady until after returning home?
ai.summary: This report gives a legal ruling concerning the mutamattiʿ who did not find the hady and forgot the three days of fasting. It explains that if Dhū al-Ḥijjah has passed, he must offer blood, while the report allowing ten days of fasting after returning home applies to one who returned before the end of Dhū al-Ḥijjah.
